context: Coerce and validate where the value ENTERS the adapter, in __init__, not at the point of use, so every consumer of the attribute sees an already-safe value and a later call site cannot reintroduce the hole. thread_limit: int() it and raise a ValueError naming the option when it is not integral. memory_limit and max_temp_directory_size: prefer DuckDB's parameterised SET where the pinned version supports it; where it does not, validate against the same bounded memory-size pattern MCP already applies (benchbox/mcp/schemas.py MEMORY_LIMIT_PATTERN) before interpolating. Fix all three in one pass -- leaving two of three hardened is a worse state than none, because it implies the file was reviewed.
description:
benchbox/platforms/duckdb.py:667 reads `self.thread_limit = config.get('thread_limit')` with no coercion, and :800 applies it as `conn.execute(f'SET threads TO {self.thread_limit}')` -- raw interpolation of a config-supplied value into SQL. Two sibling settings have the same shape: :790 `SET memory_limit = '{self.memory_limit}'` and :795 `SET max_temp_directory_size = '{self.max_temp_directory_size}'`.

This is a consequence of my own change and I am logging it against myself. Before #1514, DuckDBAdapter.from_config omitted `thread_limit` from its pass-through key list, so the only way to reach :800 was to construct the adapter directly. Adding it to that list -- which is what made MCP's duckdb.threads actually apply -- also connected the unified-config and config-file paths to the interpolation.

NOT an MCP escalation: MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_ALLOWLIST bounds duckdb.threads to an int in 1..256 and _prepare_adapter_platform_options renames it, so nothing string-shaped survives that boundary. The exposure is the non-MCP path -- a benchmark config or profile YAML carrying `thread_limit: '4; ATTACH ...'` is interpolated verbatim. Config files are comparatively trusted, hence medium.

WHY THIS IS SEQUENCED FIRST IN THE DUCKDB CHAIN: [duckdb-from-config-drops-constructor-read-keys] proposes adding `max_temp_directory_size` and `progress_bar` to the same pass-through list. Doing that before this hardening lands repeats the exact mistake #1514 made -- it makes :795's unhardened f-string live from config. That item is blocked on this one.

Identified 2026-08-04 during the adversarial review of the mcp-v2-platform-options batch.

SUPERSEDES `duckdb-thread-limit-raw-sql-interpolation`, which was dropped minutes after creation on 2026-08-04 to attach anti-patterns, sequenced work units, prior art and dependency edges. `drop` is a soft state change rather than a delete, so the original id could not be reused; the dropped item carries the reason and links back here.

anti_patterns.dont: fix this by escaping or quote-doubling the interpolated string
anti_patterns.instead: validate and coerce once in __init__ so the attribute itself is trustworthy
anti_patterns.why: escaping is a defence against one syntax at one call site and silently rots when a fourth SET statement is added; it also leaves the attribute holding an unvalidated value for every other reader

anti_patterns.dont: harden thread_limit alone because it is the one this batch touched
anti_patterns.instead: fix all three interpolations in one change
anti_patterns.why: memory_limit and max_temp_directory_size share the identical shape, and a partial pass signals to the next reader that the file was already reviewed and is safe

anti_patterns.dont: import benchbox.mcp from benchbox.platforms to reuse MEMORY_LIMIT_PATTERN
anti_patterns.instead: lift the pattern into a shared location below both, or duplicate it with a comment pointing at the source of truth
anti_patterns.why: it inverts the layering (surfaces sit above platforms) and would make an MCP-scoped policy constant load-bearing for CLI runs

anti_patterns.dont: narrow the MCP allow-list bound to compensate for the adapter accepting anything
anti_patterns.instead: harden the adapter, and leave the MCP bound exactly where it is
anti_patterns.why: MCP is already the tightest path and is not the exposed one; tightening it hides the real gap on the config-file path and makes the adapter look safe when it is not

preserves.behavior: An absent thread_limit still means 'emit no SET threads at all', not 'emit a default'
Existing DuckDB adapter defaults are unchanged when no key is supplied (memory_limit still defaults to 4GB)

the SET block carries three raw f-string interpolations of adapter config; supersede all three in one pass rather than hardening only the one this batch touched
